issues.description: Constructor parameter ordering for Course is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement shows and the template declares an initializer with parameters (name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) and even gives an example call Course(name: ..., instructor: ..., ratings: ...). The solution's Course implementation, however, declares the initializer as init(instructor: String, name: String, ratings: [Int]), which reverses the first two parameter labels. This mismatch between the expected initializer signature and the solution implementation can confuse students about the correct parameter labels/order to use and may lead to call-site errors or uncertainty when implementing the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course initializer parameter labels and order consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Prefer the form shown in the problem/example: init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) and update the solution's Course implementation to use that signature (or alternatively adjust the problem/template to match the solution, but keeping the name-first order is clearer and matches the example usage in Client.swift). Ensure all call sites (Client.swift and tests) use the same parameter labels and order.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template show the Course initializer as Course(name:instructor:ratings:). In the solution the initializer is declared with the parameter labels in a different order (init(instructor:name:ratings:)). Although Swift call sites can use labels in any order, this difference in the initializer signature ordering creates a small conceptual mismatch between the problem/example and the provided solution that may confuse students trying to map the example invocation to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer parameter order consistent with the problem statement and template by declaring the solution initializer as init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) so the example call Course(name:..., instructor:..., ratings:...) directly matches the implementation.
